history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Reproduce the confirmed SparseArray.astype sparse->dense accuracy failure by reconstructing E_B/E_F (build/env) so pandas sparse astype tests fail on buggy and pass on fixed without changing T_dev.
assumptions: A failing -k/FILE test corresponds to the uint64 dense exact case and/or boxed datetimelike fill value case in the pandas sparse astype suite.

The harness bug is triggered purely by pandas code path (SparseArray.astype dense-target densification) and not by external numerical libraries; thus only building with appropriate Python/NumPy versions is needed to make the failure manifest consistently.
No code changes to pandas are allowed; only rebuilding environments/versions (E_B/E_F) and build recipe/config are allowed.

actions.step: Verify interpreters/versions used by each checkout venv (no import from checkout root).
actions.command: cd /tmp && (python -V) && python -c "import numpy as np, pandas as pd; print('np', np.__version__); print('pd', pd.__version__)"

actions.step: Build both buggy and fixed revisions with the same recipe but with a NumPy version likely to surface the float64 rounding from Python-int uint64 fill_value (target: ensure float64 rounding above 2**53 is representable as observed).
Run only the targeted sparse astype test case that must fail on buggy and pass on fixed.
Run the same targeted case on fixed.
If uint64 case unexpectedly passes on buggy, run the boxed datetimelike fill case instead (still the same file + -k to avoid broad collection).

plans.success_criterion: For the selected sparse astype test case, the developer test suite transition must show: FAIL on buggy revision with a real assertion/expected-value mismatch (not collection/import error), and PASS on fixed revision with the correct densification behavior (no silent uint64 rounding / no boxed datetimelike object/raw-int mangling).
